## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac.** 3-bets extremely wide — includes mid pocket pairs and trash. Calls down light. Folds to 3-bets from tight players. **Postflop TWO LINES**: (1) **Air line**: c-bets flop then checks/folds turn when called — profitable float spot. (2) **Medium-strength line**: checks flop then bets turn = real hand (not a bluff, delayed value). **Exploit**: 3-bet for value. Value bet thin. Do NOT bluff. Float flop c-bets. Fold ace-high to check-flop/bet-turn line.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled.** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium (suited aces as semi-bluffs). Actively 3-bets from SB vs late-position steals. **Postflop**: Checks draws on flop, leads turn when completing. River checks can be traps. Folds dry boards without connections. **Exploit**: C-bet dry boards. Turn leads after flop checks = completed draw. Don't value-bet thin on river. Can call wider vs 4-bets. Tighten steals when P3 in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~47%), passive preflop, #1 chip accumulator across sessions.** Limps weak, raises better. 3-bets 99+, shoves AA. **EXTREMELY sticky** — confirmed calling river with 9-high and bottom pair. Strong hand lines: check-raises AND donk-bets (especially as non-PFA on favorable boards). **Exploit**: Isolate limps with position. Value bet EXTREMELY wide — #1 value target. NEVER bluff. Respect check-raises and donk-bets as strength.

**Player 5**: **Ultra-nit (~6% VPIP) but highly effective.** Any preflop raise = extreme premium. Donk-bets made hands (folds to raises/turn barrels). With strong draws: donk-bets AND shoves. **Exploit**: Fold to preflop aggression unless premium. Two-barrel bluffs effective. Cautious raising donk-bets on draw-heavy boards.

**Player 6**: **Tight raiser (~9%) with wide limping/calling range.** 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. Flat-calls with TT-JJ/AQ and small pairs; folds non-premium to 3-bets. **Donk-bets wide (including underpairs).** Extremely sticky on dry boards. **KEY WEAKNESS**: Folds QQ/KK on ace-high boards and folds to double-barrels on scary turns. **Exploit**: Fold to 3-bets/4-bets. Isolate limps freely. Don't bluff dry boards. DO bluff ace-high boards and scary turn cards.

**Player 7**: **Wider preflop than TAG — calls with broadways and wide from blinds.** Passive preflop but AGGRESSIVE postflop — donk-leads and double-barrels with strength. Raises flop with just top pair on paired boards (spewy). Once committed, calls down with one pair on scary boards. Marginal winner — slightly better than a bleeder. **Exploit**: Value bet relentlessly when ahead. Their flop raises often = just top pair. Don't bluff once they've shown aggression. Respect donk-lead + double-barrel combos.

## My Table Image & Critical Self-Assessment

**Image**: **STILL TOO LOOSE — VPIP ~40% across two sessions despite awareness.** Table does not view me as tight. This erodes fold equity for steals and light 3-bets. Knowing the leak isn't enough — must actively discipline opening range.

**Biggest session leak: Medium-strength hands.** Hands like A8o and 77 generated the session's largest losses (-210 and -120). These are the hands that look playable but create tough postflop spots multiway or vs aggression. Premium hands (QQ = +325) and steals (AJ, JTs = small wins) were profitable.

**Specific leaks**: (1) Playing/continuing with weak aces (A8o type) in raised pots = major -EV. (2) Investing significantly with mid pairs then folding = chip bleed. (3) Still calling too many flop bets with just overcards vs sticky players.

## Core Strategy for Next Session

1. **TIGHTEN DRAMATICALLY** — Target VPIP ≤25%. Cut weak aces (A8o-, K3s-type), offsuit broadways, and marginal suited connectors from open range. This is priority #1.
2. **Hand classification**: Play premiums (TT+, AJ+, KQ) for value. Play suited connectors/small pairs only in position vs limpers as set-mine/implied-odds plays. FOLD everything else preflop.
3. **Against P4**: Value bet relentlessly with any pair+. Never bluff. Isolate limps.
4. **Against P2**: Float flop c-bets (air line). Fold to check-flop/bet-turn (medium line). 3-bet for value.
5. **Against P7**: Value bet wide when ahead. Respect sustained aggression.
6. **Against P5/P6**: Fold to their preflop aggression. Bluff P5 with two barrels. Bluff P6 on ace-high boards or scary turns only.
7. **Against P3**: Tighten steals from late position. Respect 4-bets but can call wider.
8. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P4 (station accumulator) > P6 (sticky) > P5 (nit). P2 and P7 most exploitable.

**Opponent Profiles:**  
- Player 1: TAG with disciplined aggression — UTG 3-bet range confirmed as QQ+/AK only. Respect their early position 3-bets as premiums. Shows willingness to flat 3-bets in position against passive players with weaker holdings (e.g., A8o), indicating their flatting range can be wider situationally. Postflop tendency: check-folds turn after c-betting flop when facing resistance, revealing bluff-heavy c-bet frequency on dry boards. Slowplays monsters aggressively on later streets — exercise caution on paired boards when they flat flop bets.
- Player 2: Passive preflop caller with moderate EP opening range (broadways, mid pairs). High fold-to-3-bet tendency — profitable target for 3-bet bluffs, especially from late position. Confirmed: will flat EP raises with wider range than expected, but remains vulnerable to postflop pressure. Capable of 3-betting medium pocket pairs (e.g., 99) from late position against EP opens — their 3-bet range isn’t exclusively premiums.
- Player 3: Nit — EP opening range remains TT+/AQ+. Folds to 3-bets and flop aggression consistently. Highly predictable — avoid light defends against their opens without strong holdings.
- Player 4: Loose-passive station — overcalls preflop with weak aces and suited connectors. Postflop calling tendency extends to marginal pairs and draws. Limp-reraise range is premium (QQ+/AK) — fold marginal hands against this action. Preflop raises (non-limp) from middle/late positions can include strong but not premium holdings — value-heavy but wider than limp-reraise range.
- Player 6: LAG with selective aggression — opens wider from EP than nits, capable of donk-leading flop with value or strong draws. Folds to 3-bet pressure — profitable to 3-bet bluff against their late position opens. Open-limps from EP indicate weak/speculative range — isolate aggressively.
- Player 7: Tight-passive with premium-only 3-bets from SB (QQ+/AK). No light 3-betting — fold non-premiums against their 3-bets. Postflop aggression is value-driven — multi-street bets after flatting preflop indicate strong hands or nut draws. Overplays top pair good kicker — capable of calling down aggressively.

**Self-Improvement & Table Image:**  
- Image remains ultra-tight (0% VPIP this session) — reinforces credibility of future raises and 3-bets. Capitalize next session by widening opening range from late position to exploit perceived nitty image. Avoid defending light against strong 3-bettors (Player 1, Player 7) — discipline maintained this session was correct.

**Strategic Learnings:**  
- Primary exploitation targets: Player 4 (station — thin value bet and 3-bet bluff frequently), Player 2 (fold-to-3-bet tendency — apply preflop pressure).
- Key cautions: Player 1’s UTG 3-bets and Player 7’s SB 3-bets are premium-only — avoid light defends or bluffs.
- Player 6’s donk-leading requires adjusted response — consider raising with strong holdings or floating in position.

**Opponent Profiles & Tendencies:**
- **Player 1 (LAG / Spewy):** Highly aggressive and prone to overplaying. Opens extremely wide preflop from all positions (including offsuit K-high trash and weak offsuit Aces like A8o from UTG), and will even call 3-bets out of position with these weak hands. Capable of massive multi-street bluffs with pure air, and will frequently take delayed stabs when flops check through. Extremely sticky post-flop: will float flops and call turn bets with just Ace-high. *Note on nutted hands:* With absolute monsters (like top full house), they will sometimes trap by flatting a flop raise, then take the betting lead on the turn and jam the river.
- **Player 2 (Extreme LAG / Calling Station):** Plays a very wide range (will open and call 3-bets OOP with medium suited gappers/connectors) and 3-bets light from the blinds/button. Post-flop, they are an absolute station—floats very light (e.g., check-calling with bottom pair) and capable of calling river shoves on scary boards with marginal hands. They barrel marginal hands on scary boards. *Exception:* In single-raised pots defending the Big Blind, they play straightforwardly and will fold to small c-bets on dry boards.
- **Player 4 (Aggressive / Extreme Station):** High VPIP/PFR but also capable of limping absolute garbage (e.g., 97o) from middle position. Crucially, their 3-bet range includes many non-premiums, and they will fold to 4-bets, but they DO balance this by 5-bet jamming their actual premiums (AA). Post-flop, they are capable of mind-boggling spew and station behavior—they will call turn bets with weak gutshots and even call river bets with absolute air (9-high). *Note:* They do have a folding button on the river if the board becomes extremely scary (e.g., 4-to-a-straight, 3-to-a-flush) and they face heavy aggression.
- **Player 5 (Passive / Recreational):** Classic limp/caller preflop, but will open-raise strong hands. Post-flop, they make probing donk-bets. *Crucial Note:* While some donk-bets are weak, they will play strong draws (like nut flush draws) extremely aggressively, donk-betting flops and open-shoving turns. Their preflop 3-bets represent an incredibly strong premium range.
- **Player 6 (Mixed TAG/Passive):** Capable of open-limping weak offsuit broadways from early position. Their 3-bets represent a very strong, value-heavy range (premiums and AK). Post-flop, they can be sticky, floating flop donk-bets with just AK-high. They will also donk-bet flops with vulnerable marginal hands (like underpairs) to test the waters, but will shut down and check through later streets if called. Will value bet two-pair hands on the river even on flush-completing boards.
- **Player 7 (Loose / Extreme Station):** Extremely loose preflop; capable of cold-calling 3-bets out of position. Post-flop, they are an absolute calling station. They will raise flops with top pair, but more importantly, they will call massive river jams with just one pair (e.g., top pair) even on the scariest possible runouts (paired, 4-to-a-straight, flush-completing boards). They also donk-bet low/coordinated boards and make small stabs/bluffs on the river with pure air when the action checks down.

**Strategic Adjustments & Exploits:**
- **Vs. Player 1:** Widen your bluff-catching range and value-bet wider. Do not over-fold to their post-flop aggression; be prepared to call down with marginal made hands, especially when they stab at pots that check through. Exploit their wide preflop calling range by 3-betting them aggressively for value.
- **Vs. Player 2:** NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly and go for maximum value (including overbets/shoves) even on scary runouts. Do not rely on flop check-raises as bluffs, as they float very wide. In blind-vs-blind or late-position steals, small c-bets on dry boards are highly profitable.
- **Vs. Player 4:** Generally NEVER bluff them post-flop. They will call down with literal air. Value bet them relentlessly and thinly. Preflop, target them with isolation raises when they limp, and exploit their wide 3-betting range by 4-betting them (for value and as a bluff), but ALWAYS fold your 4-bet bluffs to a 5-bet jam.
- **Vs. Player 5:** Be cautious when raising their flop donk-bets on draw-heavy boards, as they are capable of shoving over the top with strong draws. Over-fold to their preflop 3-bets.
- **Vs. Player 6:** Give immense respect to their preflop aggression (3-bets), but realize their limping range is wider. You can float or call their flop donk-bets if you have equity, as they frequently shut down on the turn with weak made hands. 
- **Vs. Player 7:** NEVER bluff them post-flop. Value bet relentlessly and go for maximum value with your strong hands, as they will call down for their entire stack with just one pair on horrific boards. Respect their flop donk-bets when you have unimproved overcards, but bluff-catch their small river stabs if the hand checks down.

**Self-Image & Future Adjustments:**
- **Table Image:** Just completed an ultra-nitty session (folded 19 out of 20 hands). My image is currently extremely tight. 
- **Next Session Adjustment:** I can use this ultra-tight image to get away with more preflop steals and c-bet bluffs against observant/tighter players (like Player 6). However, I must remember that the massive stations (Players 2, 4, and 7) do not care about my image and will call down anyway. Against them, continue to play a pure, relentless value game and strictly avoid bluffing.

They **call preflop opens too wide for their postflop capabilities**, then **fold to any aggression on the flop**, especially in 3-bet pots. **Exploit**: **3-bet their opens liberally**, especially from late position; **c-bet 80%+ on dry flops** when they call; **rarely give them credit for strong hands unless they raise**.

- **Player 1** shows **light 3-betting tendencies preflop** but **extreme passivity postflop**, often **checking back strong hands** or **calling with weak pairs**. This suggests a **"trap-heavy" but non-aggressive profile**. **Exploit**: **Bet for value thinly on static boards**, **avoid overfolding to their rare aggression**, and **probe turn/river more often when checked to**.

- **Player 2** is a **preflop LAG** (high PFR) but **postflop fit-or-fold**. They **3-bet wide**, then **fold to flop c-bets unless they hit**. **Exploit**: **Call 3-bets wider in position with suited connectors or backdoor equity**, then **apply pressure on dry flops**; **avoid bluffing them on coordinated boards where they’re more likely to continue**.

- **Your table image is perceived as tight (VPIP ~21%) and highly foldable in 3-bet pots**, especially out of position. This session confirmed opponents (notably Player 4) are **leveraging large flop leads to exploit your perceived tightness**. **Strategic adjustment**: **Widen your 3-bet defense range in position** to include **Axs, KQs, QJs, and suited connectors with backdoor potential**—not just for immediate equity, but to **balance your range and reduce exploitable folding**.

- **Top pair with weak/medium kickers (ATo, AJo, KTo) is consistently unprofitable in 3-bet pots against TAGs on dry A/K-high boards**, especially when **out of position or facing large sizing**. **Refined rule**: Treat these as **bluff-catchers only against known bluffers**; otherwise, **fold unless you have strong redraws (e.g., flush/straight draws) or deep stacks (>150bb)**.

- **Passive players (Player 7, Player 3) rarely bluff on any street**, while **aggressive players (Player 4, Player 2) bluff selectively—mostly on dynamic boards, not static ones**. **General heuristic**: **On dry, static boards, assume value-heavy ranges from all opponents unless proven otherwise**.

- **Your biggest leak this session**: **Over-folding to aggression in 3-bet pots**, especially with hands that have **blocker or backdoor value**. While folding ATo was correct against Player 4, your **overall defense frequency was too low**, making your range predictable. **Next session focus**: **Defend 3-bets 10–15% wider in position**, even if just to float or check-call with equity.
